q: All waves are produced by a ____.
e: All waves are produced by a vibrating source. The physics in this sentence is built around vibrating source.

q: Wave motion is a method of transferring ____ by successive disturbances through the medium.
e: Wave motion is a method of transferring energy by successive disturbances through the medium. Energy here means the capacity to do work.

q: This movement of energy takes place without transferring ____.
e: This movement of energy takes place without transferring matter. Matter here means anything that has mass and occupies space.

q: The mechanical waves need material medium to propagate and cannot pass through ____.
e: The mechanical waves need material medium to propagate and cannot pass through vacuum. Vacuum here means a space emptied of air so electrons can travel freely in a tube.

q: Sound waves and seismic waves, which are produced by an earthquake, are ____.
e: Sound waves and seismic waves, which are produced by an earthquake, are mechanical waves. The physics in this sentence is built around mechanical waves.

q: Electromagnetic waves can pass through ____ and they do not need medium for propagation.
e: Electromagnetic waves can pass through vacuum and they do not need medium for propagation. Vacuum here means a space emptied of air so electrons can travel freely in a tube.

q: Light wave and X-rays are ____.
e: Light wave and X-rays are electromagnetic waves. The physics in this sentence is built around electromagnetic waves.

q: Waves are classified as transverse and longitudinal waves depending on ____ of particles in the medium through which they propagate.
e: Waves are classified as transverse and longitudinal waves depending on vibration of particles in the medium through which they propagate. In a longitudinal wave the particles shake along the travel, as in sound.

q: If the displacements of particles of the medium are ____ to the direction of the wave, such a wave is called a transverse wave.
e: If the displacements of particles of the medium are perpendicular to the direction of the wave, such a wave is called a transverse wave. In a transverse wave the particles shake at right angles to the travel.

q: Waves in a vibrating string are ____.
e: Waves in a vibrating string are transverse waves. In a transverse wave the particles shake at right angles to the travel.

q: Light waves and other electromagnetic waves are also ____.
e: Light waves and other electromagnetic waves are also transverse waves. In a transverse wave the particles shake at right angles to the travel.

q: If the displacements of particles of medium are ____ to the direction of the waves, such a wave is called a longitudinal wave.
e: If the displacements of particles of medium are parallel to the direction of the waves, such a wave is called a longitudinal wave. In a longitudinal wave the particles shake along the travel, as in sound.

q: Compressional waves in a slinky coiled spring and sound waves are ____.
e: Compressional waves in a slinky coiled spring and sound waves are longitudinal waves. In a longitudinal wave the particles shake along the travel, as in sound.

q: The highest and the lowest points which show the maximum displacement of vibrating particle from its rest position (or) equilibrium line are called ____ respectively.
e: The highest and the lowest points which show the maximum displacement of vibrating particle from its rest position (or) equilibrium line are called wave crest and wave trough respectively. Wave crest and wave trough here means a travelling disturbance that carries energy, not the medium itself. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The distance between any two consecutive wave crests (or) two consecutive wave troughs is called ____.
e: The distance between any two consecutive wave crests (or) two consecutive wave troughs is called wavelength. Wavelength here means the distance from one crest to the next crest. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.

q: The unit of wavelength in SI unit is ____.
e: The unit of wavelength in SI unit is metre (m). SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.

q: Generally the wavelength is the distance between two nearest points of ____.
e: Generally the wavelength is the distance between two nearest points of same phase. Same phase here means lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.

q: The number of complete waves passing a point per second of a vibrating source is also called ____.
e: The number of complete waves passing a point per second of a vibrating source is also called frequency. Frequency here means how many complete waves pass a point each second. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: The SI unit of frequency is ____.
e: The SI unit of frequency is hertz (Hz). SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: One hertz is equal to ____.
e: One hertz is equal to one complete cycle per second. The physics in this sentence is built around one complete cycle per second.

q: The time taken by the wave to travel the distance between any two consecutive wave crests (or) the time required for one complete vibration is called ____ of a wave.
e: The time taken by the wave to travel the distance between any two consecutive wave crests (or) the time required for one complete vibration is called period of a wave. Period here means the time for one complete vibration.

q: The unit of period is the ____.
e: The unit of period is the second (s). The unit that belongs with this quantity is second (s).

q: The period is the ____ of the frequency.
e: The period is the reciprocal or inverse of the frequency. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: The amplitude of a wave is the ____ of displacement of vibrating particle.
e: The amplitude of a wave is the maximum value of displacement of vibrating particle. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: Velocity of wave is the ____ with which a wave crest travels.
e: Velocity of wave is the speed with which a wave crest travels. Speed here means how fast the path length changes, with no direction. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The unit of wave velocity is ____.
e: The unit of wave velocity is metre per second ($\text{m s}^{-1}$). Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Most of the periodic waves are represented by ____ graphs.
e: Most of the periodic waves are represented by sine (or) cosine graphs. The physics in this sentence is built around sine (or) cosine.

q: The relationship between the frequency, wavelength and velocity of a periodic wave can be obtained by ____.
e: The relationship between the frequency, wavelength and velocity of a periodic wave can be obtained by $v = f \lambda$. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: A displacement-distance graph describes the displacement of all particles at a ____.
e: A displacement-distance graph describes the displacement of all particles at a particular instant of time. Particular instant of time here means the duration of an event, not the distance moved along a force. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: Note that displacement of particle is plotted on ____ and distance moved by the wave is on x-axis.
e: Note that displacement of particle is plotted on y-axis and distance moved by the wave is on x-axis. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: A displacement-time graph describes the displacement of particle of a certain position as a ____ taken to travel by a wave.
e: A displacement-time graph describes the displacement of particle of a certain position as a function of time taken to travel by a wave. Function of time here means the duration of an event, not the distance moved along a force. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The surface that joins all the points of same phase is called ____.
e: The surface that joins all the points of same phase is called wavefront. Wavefront names the surface that joins all the points of same phase.

q: When a series of wave strike an obstacle, they are ____.
e: When a series of wave strike an obstacle, they are turned back. The physics in this sentence is built around turned back.

q: This turning back of waves is called ____.
e: This turning back of waves is called reflection. Reflection here means light bouncing back from a surface.

q: When waves strike a ____, the waves are reflected from the barrier.
e: When waves strike a straight barrier, the waves are reflected from the barrier. Straight barrier here means the path light takes in a uniform medium.

q: The angle of incidence is equal to the ____.
e: The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. Angle of reflection here means light bouncing back from a surface.

q: The wavelength and velocity of the wave remain ____ in reflection of wave.
e: The wavelength and velocity of the wave remain constant in reflection of wave. Constant here means a quantity that does not change, not the agreed measuring unit. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.

q: The speed of water waves depends on the ____.
e: The speed of water waves depends on the depth of water. The physics in this sentence is built around depth of water.

q: It ____ when the depth of water becomes less deep.
e: It decreases when the depth of water becomes less deep. The physics in this sentence is built around decreases.

q: When water waves pass from deep to shallow water the velocity of wave is ____ and the wavelength is shorter or vice-versa.
e: When water waves pass from deep to shallow water the velocity of wave is lesser and the wavelength is shorter or vice-versa. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: When waves are incident to the boundary with an angle, the ____ of the waves changes.
e: When waves are incident to the boundary with an angle, the direction of the waves changes. The physics in this sentence is built around direction.

q: Such a change in direction is called ____.
e: Such a change in direction is called refraction. Refraction here means light bending as it changes medium. Light bends toward the normal when it slows down in the new medium.

q: It can be noticed that in refraction, the wavelength and velocity change but ____ remains the same.
e: It can be noticed that in refraction, the wavelength and velocity change but frequency remains the same. Frequency here means how many complete waves pass a point each second. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.

q: Diffraction is the ____ from the straight-on direction through a gap (or) moves around an obstacle.
e: Diffraction is the spreading of waves from the straight-on direction through a gap (or) moves around an obstacle. The physics in this sentence is built around spreading of waves.

q: The wave that passes the edges of the gap of the obstacle ____.
e: The wave that passes the edges of the gap of the obstacle spread out. The physics in this sentence is built around spread out.

q: The wider the gap, the ____ the waves spread out.
e: The wider the gap, the less the waves spread out. The physics in this sentence is built around less.

q: The narrower the gap, the ____ the waves spread out.
e: The narrower the gap, the more the waves spread out. The physics in this sentence is built around more.

q: Sound is a form of ____ that is transferred from one place to another in a certain medium.
e: Sound is a form of energy that is transferred from one place to another in a certain medium. Energy here means the capacity to do work.

q: Sound wave is produced by a ____ placed in a medium.
e: Sound wave is produced by a vibrating object placed in a medium. The physics in this sentence is built around vibrating object.

q: The pressure changes occur ____ in the medium by vibrating object.
e: The pressure changes occur alternately in the medium by vibrating object. The same force on a smaller area means a larger pressure.

q: Sound wave propagates as a series of ____ like longitudinal waves on a vibrating spring.
e: Sound wave propagates as a series of compression and rarefaction like longitudinal waves on a vibrating spring. In a longitudinal wave the particles shake along the travel, as in sound.

q: Unlike electromagnetic waves, sound waves need a ____ to propagate.
e: Unlike electromagnetic waves, sound waves need a medium to propagate. The physics in this sentence is built around medium.

q: Sound wave cannot travel through ____.
e: Sound wave cannot travel through vacuum. Vacuum here means a space emptied of air so electrons can travel freely in a tube.

q: The compression is created in the medium as the vibrating object ____.
e: The compression is created in the medium as the vibrating object pushes molecules together. The physics in this sentence is built around pushes molecules together.

q: The compression region has ____.
e: The compression region has higher pressure. Higher pressure here means force acting normally on unit area. The same force on a smaller area means a larger pressure.

q: When the object moves back, the molecules are spread out and ____ is created and the pressure of that region is low.
e: When the object moves back, the molecules are spread out and rarefaction is created and the pressure of that region is low. The same force on a smaller area means a larger pressure.

q: The average person can only hear sound that has a frequency higher than ____ and lower than $20\,000 \text{ Hz}$.
e: The average person can only hear sound that has a frequency higher than $20 \text{ Hz}$ and lower than $20\,000 \text{ Hz}$. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: This interval of frequency is called the ____ (or) hearing range.
e: This interval of frequency is called the audible range (or) hearing range. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: Sound waves with frequencies greater than $20\,000 \text{ Hz}$ are called ____.
e: Sound waves with frequencies greater than $20\,000 \text{ Hz}$ are called ultrasounds. Ultrasounds names sound waves with frequencies greater than $20\,000 \text{ Hz}$.

q: Some objects vibrating with frequencies under $20 \text{ Hz}$ produces sound which cannot be heard by ____.
e: Some objects vibrating with frequencies under $20 \text{ Hz}$ produces sound which cannot be heard by human. The physics in this sentence is built around human.

q: This is called ____.
e: This is called infrasound. Infrasound names this.

q: Generally, the speed of sound depends on the ____ of the medium.
e: Generally, the speed of sound depends on the density of the medium. Density here means mass per unit volume. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: The denser the medium is, the ____ the speed because the particles of the medium are tightly bound together.
e: The denser the medium is, the greater the speed because the particles of the medium are tightly bound together. The physics in this sentence is built around greater.

q: At $0^{\circ}\text{C}$ the speed of sound in air is ____.
e: At $0^{\circ}\text{C}$ the speed of sound in air is $332 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $332 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

q: Whenever the air temperature increases by $1^{\circ}\text{C}$, speed of sound will increase by ____.
e: Whenever the air temperature increases by $1^{\circ}\text{C}$, speed of sound will increase by $0.2\%$. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The speed of sound in air can be expressed as ____.
e: The speed of sound in air can be expressed as $v = 332 \sqrt{\frac{T}{273}}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $v = 332 \sqrt{\frac{T}{273}}$.

q: Here $T$ is given in ____ and $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
e: Here $T$ is given in K and $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$. The physics in this sentence is built around K.

q: The above relation can be approximated by ____.
e: The above relation can be approximated by $v = 332 + 0.6(T - 273)$. The physics in this sentence is built around $v = 332 + 0.6(T - 273)$.

q: In air medium, the speed of sound increases by ____ with temperature rise by one degree ($1^{\circ}\text{C}$ or $1\text{K}$).
e: In air medium, the speed of sound increases by $0.6 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ with temperature rise by one degree ($1^{\circ}\text{C}$ or $1\text{K}$). Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.
